name: a retry wrapper reports the argument defaults of the callable it wraps
expected_behavior: __defaults__ and __kwdefaults__ read off a retry-decorated callable (sync or async) equal what the undecorated callable reports, while the usual wrapper metadata stays intact

name: a deadline-bounded stop condition gives up before overrunning its budget
expected_behavior: stop_before_delay(D) stops at the last attempt whose elapsed time plus the upcoming pause is still under D, so total requested delay never reaches D; stop_after_delay keeps overrunning and stop_after_attempt is unchanged

name: coroutine before/after/before-sleep hooks are awaited on the async path
expected_behavior: coroutine before / after / before_sleep hooks run in the same order and with the same attempt numbers as the equivalent plain hooks, which keep working

name: a coroutine retry predicate decides the async loop instead of being treated as truthy
expected_behavior: an async retried function with a coroutine retry= predicate stops as soon as the predicate resolves to false and returns the last result, exactly like a plain predicate

name: a bare package import does not load the asyncio machinery
expected_behavior: in a fresh interpreter, importing the package leaves asyncio out of sys.modules while the asynchronous retrying entry point and the synchronous names stay reachable from the package root

name: a callable object whose call is a coroutine is dispatched to the async retry path
expected_behavior: decorating an instance whose __call__ is a coroutine produces an awaitable that retries the body until it succeeds; plain sync and plain async targets keep their existing dispatch

name: predicate retry strategies accept coroutines and compose with the synchronous ones
expected_behavior: tenacity.asyncio.retry provides retry_if_result / retry_if_exception over coroutine predicates, and combining a synchronous strategy with an asynchronous one via | yields a strategy the async loop evaluates; purely synchronous composition is unchanged

name: the built-in backoff pause follows whichever async library is running
expected_behavior: a retried coroutine with a non-zero wait completes under Trio with no sleep function configured, still completes under asyncio, and an explicitly supplied pause function is still the one used

name: a decorated function publishes the statistics of its own last run
expected_behavior: fn.statistics reports the attempts the latest call took (sync and async) and is refreshed per call, while fn.retry stays the patchable configuration object and retry_with keeps working

name: the randomised exponential backoff window is bounded below as well as above
expected_behavior: every pause produced by the randomised exponential strategy configured with min M and max X lies in [M, X], the window still widens with the attempt number, and the deterministic exponential strategy is unchanged

name: the pre-sleep log line renders the upcoming delay as a readable number
expected_behavior: a combined wait of 0.1 + 0.2 logs 'in 0.3 seconds' by default, a supplied sec_format renders the delay with it, and the rest of the line is unchanged

name: the backoff delay can be derived from the exception that was raised
expected_behavior: wait_exception(predicate) passes the raised exception to the predicate once per failed attempt and uses the returned number as that attempt's pause; the established wait strategies are untouched

name: coroutine wait and stop strategies steer the async retry loop
expected_behavior: a coroutine wait= strategy determines each pause and a coroutine stop= strategy decides when to give up, matching what the equivalent plain callables produce

name: a coroutine give-up callback supplies the caller's fallback value
expected_behavior: when the attempt budget is exhausted on the async path, a coroutine retry_error_callback runs and the value it produces is what the caller receives; a plain callback behaves the same way

name: the post-attempt log line preserves the magnitude of the elapsed time
expected_behavior: an elapsed time of 0.0025 s round-trips out of the rendered line to within a tenth of a percent, a sub-millisecond elapsed time is not rendered as zero, and an explicit seconds format is honoured verbatim

name: an awaitable pause function makes the whole retry loop awaitable
expected_behavior: with an awaitable pause function a synchronous retried callable yields an awaitable whose pauses are actually performed; with a blocking pause function the call stays synchronous and unchanged
